tracks.title: Theme: Rain on the Loft Window
tracks.note: The theme, stated plainly in E-flat: A, A, B, A, an electric piano chorus, B, A, ending on the IV. Brushes, fretless, reed lead, muted trumpet, vibraphone answers, the rain before and after.

tracks.title: Var. I: Espresso, Two Sugars
tracks.note: The theme in F, as a light shuffle: the motto traded between vibraphone and suitcase piano (once as written, once upside down), the flute an eighth late, muted trumpet on B, two choruses, a stop-time.

tracks.title: Var. II: Taxi Lights on Wet Asphalt
tracks.note: The theme in G at 104 bpm, every long note pushed a sixteenth early: slap bass, a plucked guitar in sixteenths, synth brass, the reed with a polysynth an octave above; two choruses; up to A-flat at the end.

tracks.title: Var. III: Elevator to the 23rd Floor
tracks.note: A bossa nova in B-flat at 120 bpm with the theme in augmentation (every note twice as long) on flute; a nylon-style guitar on a two-bar pattern, the glass piano on B, the motto traded in double time.

tracks.title: Var. IV: Answering Machine, 1:12 a.m.
tracks.note: The theme in C minor at 72 bpm, lo-fi: a worn tape electric piano, a close muted trumpet, a far flute, swung drums, vinyl and rain; the phone rings twice, the machine answers, nobody speaks.

tracks.title: Var. V: Neon Waltz
tracks.note: The theme in waltz time (each bar becomes two) in A-flat at 120: glass piano, folk harp, pizzicato bass, brushes, a music box; a harmonica takes it a tone higher; B on strings.

tracks.title: Var. VI: Paganini Takes the Last Train
tracks.note: A minor at 112 on a train groove. Opens with the first figure of Paganini's Caprice No. 24 (1817, public domain) and the theme answering in the minor; B in C major; the caprice in the bass turns into the theme's pick-up; ends in A major as the train leaves.

tracks.title: Var. VII: The Loft, Inverted
tracks.note: The slow heart: the theme inverted in D-flat at 66, re-harmonised; soft piano alone, then violins and cellos, choir and glass piano on the inverted B, a climax a tone higher with horns, the piano alone again.

tracks.title: Var. VIII: Couch Fort Disco
tracks.note: Four on the floor in E at 118: the theme in diminution (eight bars in four) on polysynth, then at its own speed on the reed; octave bass, clavinet, string runs, claps, congas, a wordless vocoder choir; it fades.

tracks.title: Var. IX: Steam and Static
tracks.note: The interlude, in G-flat at 60 with no drums: grain clouds made from the steam wand, the rain and the glass piano follow the harmony; the theme crosses once on the crystal bell, every note twice as long.

tracks.title: Var. X: Last Call at the Listening Bar
tracks.note: Jazz-funk in D-flat at 88, swung: the theme over tritone substitutions, sixteen bars of electric piano, reed and piano trading fours, B on strings, the last A a semitone up; glasses on the counter.

tracks.title: Finale: Dawn over the Bay, Deprogrammed
tracks.note: The theme comes home in E-flat with the night around it (the inversion as a counter-line, the motto traded, the fast version), the caprice figure as a hinge into F, everything pushed and full, then the motto slowly on the bell; the first track ended on the IV, this one on the I, as the birds start.
